pew: The player's gun. Fires several times per second for minutes at a time — must be tight, dry, characterful, and absolutely non-fatiguing. The quietest sound in the game by design.
hop: Downward-shot recoil off the ground that launches the player UP: a light, springy upward gesture. Fired often.
boost: Mid-air downward-shot boost: an airy thrust whoosh with some body, bigger than hop but still short. Fired often.
burst: Slide-burst: the one shot that shoves the player HORIZONTALLY. Should feel like a physical low shove/kick with weight, not a laser.
coin: Pickup collect: a bright inharmonic sparkle-ping with a fast decay. Must pierce a busy mix (kills + landings on the same frame) without shrillness. Plays constantly — must stay delightful.
hurt: Player takes damage: a falling, crunchy, slightly ugly hit that can NEVER be confused with any weapon sound. Attention-grabbing but not painful.
ded: Player death: the only melodic jingle in the set — a short descending phrase, properly sad, with a small tail. Plays at a full-stop moment so it can breathe.
killpop: Enemy kill confirm: plays hundreds of times per run. Tight, juicy, instantly readable pop with zero tail. The most repetition-critical sound after pew.
bosshit: Boss taking a hit from the player: a thump with real low-end body, deliberately NO sharp transient click (it lands on the same frame as the player's own fire).
bossdown: Boss defeated: THE payoff moment, the one big sound in the game. Explosion plus a feeling of triumph; a tail is welcome. Rare, so it can be long and rich.
minionpop: Boss-summoned minion death: a smaller, higher, lighter cousin of the kill pop — must be audibly 'not a real kill'. Very short.
uiclick: Menu/UI interaction: soft and tactile, felt more than heard. Like a high-quality physical button. Must never grate after dozens of menu presses.
